title: The Sweep and the Noble Lady

keywords: the sweep and the noble lady
full_text:
In Baghdad lived a humble chimney sweep named Ali, whose skin and garments were permanently blackened by soot. He earned only a few copper coins each day cleaning the hearths and chimneys of the grand mansions, yet his heart was clean, and he never touched a coin that was not his own.

One morning, Ali was summoned to clean the wide marble fireplace in the private salon of a noble lady of the Abbasid court. While scraping the soot from the flue, his brush struck a loose brick inside the chimney wall. Dislodging the brick, a velvet jewelry case fell out and landed at his feet.

Ali opened the case and caught his breath: inside rested a diamond necklace of immense value, sparkling like stars against the black soot. The salon was empty; no one had seen him discover it, and the dust on the box proved it had been hidden for years.

Ali held the case in his soot-stained hands. A voice within whispered: 'Take it! With this single jewel, you and your children will be wealthy forever; you will never scrape a chimney again.'

Ali closed the lid firmly, shook his head, and replied to his conscience: 'Wealth bought by theft is blackened with a soot that water can never wash clean.'

He carried the case downstairs and handed it directly to the noble lady. The lady gasped with astonishment: the necklace was an ancestral heirloom lost twenty years earlier during a fire, and she had long mourned its loss.

'O sweep!' cried the lady. 'You could have hidden this beneath your tunic, and no soul would have known! Why did you return it?'

Ali bowed humbly: 'I am a poor man, my lady, but my father taught me that honesty is a treasure that thieves cannot steal and fire cannot burn.'

Moved to tears by his integrity, the noble lady gifted Ali a thousand gold dinars, purchased him a comfortable house, and made him the chief steward of her estates, proving that a pure heart shines brighter than the rarest diamond.
moral: Honesty in the face of poverty and temptation is the truest badge of nobility.
